subject: research/garment-twonodeheld
professional: a thermal-comfort and clothing-thermophysiology researcher who knows the Gagge two-node model and ISO 7730 / ASHRAE 55 (the kind who reviews for Building and Environment or Energy and Buildings), reading with a control engineer's eye on the hysteresis thermostat. Not a cloth-simulation or robotic-garment-manipulation reviewer: the project models heat balance of a person wearing an infrared-gating textile, not fabric mechanics. They would check first that the two-node model matches pythermalcomfort, that the comfort proxy's target is right for the activity level, and whether 'held-out rooms' is a real generalisation test or one the setup guarantees

evidence.correctness: Every headline number reproduces and recomputes. Rerun: `cd research/garment-twonodeheld && /usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py` (4.1 s, needs scipy, which the bare python3 lacked) is byte-identical to the committed experiments/results.txt (diff empty). Independent script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5126774c-bade-554d-9a1e-517d514005d7/scratchpad/held/indep.py re-implements the 'ours' two-node model, hysteresis gate, proxy, four-schedule oracle and the 54-band tuning from the documented equations (Gagge 1986 two-node, ISO 7730 f_cl and 3.96e-8 radiation constant) with its own bisection root finder instead of scipy brentq, and imports nothing from the repository. It gives: tuned band (33.6, 33.7), train mean 0.880, 4 of 54 bands within 0.02 C; tuned/default/closed/open means 0.880/0.834/1.354, 0.935/0.882/1.405, 1.104/1.068/1.557, 1.575/1.520/2.056; oracle 0.920/0.825/1.364; switch counts tuned [1,2,1,2,14,24,1,1], default [1,2,1,2,0,0,1,1]. External tool check of the 'ref' choice set: pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 two_nodes_gagge (pip-installed in a scratch venv) at tau=0, 60 min, 0.5 clo, 50% rh, 0.1 m/s gives tsk/tcr 33.4028/36.8313 (24 C, 1 met), 33.7296/36.9444 (22 C, 2 met), 34.3273/36.8615 (28 C, 1 met), 31.3475/36.8156 (20 C, 1 met); the repository's flex.run(opts=REF) gives the same to 1e-4. Not 4: the 'ref' gate numbers were reproduced only by the package's own run (no independent ref reimplementation), and the proxy target is a modelling choice I question under domain.

evidence.craft: Read src/garment_twonodeheld/held.py (41 lines), tests/test_held.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, and the upstream met.py, switch.py, flex.py. Small, readable, deterministic, docstrings state the protocol. Defects: imports work only by sys.path.insert into three sibling research directories (held.py:5, met.py:6-7, switch.py:5) and pyproject declares only numpy and scipy, so the package does not install or run outside this tree; tests are not unittest-discoverable; run.py recomputes mean_score for every band twice (tune, then the 0.02 C sensitivity at run.py:31) and calls private module attributes through h.met.sw; warnings are globally silenced in run.py:5.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and my recomputation: the results table (README:23-32) is exact; 'beats untuned by 0.01 to 0.06 C' (0.048, 0.051, 0.059, 0.014: true); oracle comparisons 0.009 worse / 0.010 better (ours) and 0.024 better / equal (ref): true; 'both choice sets pick the same band, 0.1 C wide': true; '4 of 54 and 2 of 54 within 0.02 C': true; switch counts: true; '20 C (ref) all gates and fixed closed score the same' (1.876, 1.574): true. Limits are explicit and honest (stylised, zero lag and cost, coarse grid, narrowest width chosen after widening, proxy not a comfort index), and the 'Citation check' line says Zhang et al. (2019) was not re-read. Minor problems: the headline 'carries over' rests on mean gaps of 0.01 to 0.06 C over 4 scenarios and does not say the tuned band loses on some held-out scenarios (ref 23 C 2->1: 0.515 vs default 0.483; ours 28 C 2->1: 0.798 vs open 0.795); README:37 'that was not run' is stale since garment-twonodelag ran it.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher deciding whether a thermostat band for an infrared-gating garment can be tuned once and reused. The protocol is runnable and the numbers are right, but the result is guaranteed by the setup: the score is mean |tsk - 33.7| and the gate acts on tsk, so the best band is the one that brackets 33.7 whatever the room, and a held-out room cannot move it. My finer grid (lows every 0.05 C, widths 0.02/0.05/0.1; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5126774c-bade-554d-9a1e-517d514005d7/scratchpad/held/indep.py) picks 33.70-33.72 with train 0.873, between 0.828, outside 1.341: the optimum collapses toward a zero-width bang-bang controller at the setpoint, the textbook answer for a free, instant, wear-free actuator. Nearest prior work: Zhang et al. 2019 (Science, dynamic infrared gating textile) and Hsu et al. 2016 (Science, nanoPE personal thermal management) for the textile; Gagge, Fobelets & Berglund 1986 for the model; relay/hysteresis control and the chatter-versus-error trade-off for the controller; personal comfort systems (e.g. Vesely & Zeiler 2014 review) for model-based garment or local conditioning control. None of the control or comfort-system literature is cited and no novelty is claimed, but none exists either: it is a ~40-line step in a chain of 45 garment-* slugs, not in any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md, which the research brief says should be steps inside a programme.
evidence.domain: The underlying model is faithful to pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 (checked above), which a thermophysiologist would accept for a stylised study. They would not sign off the proxy: a fixed 33.7 C skin target regardless of activity departs from the comfort relation the repository's own base.py uses (Fanger / ISO 7730: tsk = 35.7 - 0.028 M, i.e. 34.07 C at 1 met and 32.44 C at 2 met), so half of every scenario is scored against the wrong target. With that met-dependent target (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5126774c-bade-554d-9a1e-517d514005d7/scratchpad/held/fanger.py, my reimplementation) the same band still wins, but all errors roughly double (tuned 1.603/1.576/1.975) and the 'outside' advantage over the untuned band falls from 0.051 to 0.001 C. They would also note differences of 0.01 C are below any skin-temperature sensor's resolution and any sensation threshold, and that zero lag, zero cost and 24 switches in 3 h are not a realistic actuator (disclosed).

verdict: A correct, honest, very small step. Every 'ours' number I recomputed with an independent reimplementation (own solver, no repository imports) matches results.txt to 3 dp, the experiment reproduces byte-for-byte in 4 s, and the 'ref' model matches pythermalcomfort 4.6.1 to 1e-4. It misses the bar on verification: the 4 tests are invisible to unittest and to CI, and 5 of 7 seeded mutants survive. As research it is below the PhD bar: the held-out 'carry-over' is built into the setup (the score's target is the gate's threshold variable, and a finer grid collapses the band onto the setpoint), the fixed 33.7 C target departs from the ISO 7730 activity-dependent comfort skin temperature, and the headline effect is 0.01 to 0.06 C.
